svg.title: How a verdict is reached
svg.desc: Live demod reports and 7-day baselines feed four checks: is the input stressed, has it lasted 3 reports, are sides A and B both degraded, and is a co-channel path on the channel ducting. Co-channel paths and their latest ducting feed the fourth check. Passing all four gives CCI confirmed; each failed check leads to clean, not yet, single_side or unpaired, or dual_unexplained or dual_ducting_unknown.
svg.text: The evidence the correlator combines for each LRF and RF channel, and the four checks every report goes through
ABOUT ONCE A MINUTE PER INPUT
MER, Pre-FEC BER, input power and lock
from each input, side A and side B
Median Pre-FEC BER and MER of each input
Every same-channel FCC station within 200 mi,
and the latest ducting along each path
USED IF THE LATEST POLL IS
BER at least 10 × its effective baseline, or saturated;
MER at least 3 dB below its median; or lock lost
Has it lasted 3 reports in a row?
Degraded after 3 anomalous reports, clear after 3 clean ones.
A missing minute counts neither way; a gap over 3 min restarts.
Are side A and side B both degraded?
Both report within the last 90 s. One antenna feed, two demods:
both degraded means the received signal. A dark frame never counts.
Is a co-channel path on this channel ducting?
Any path with dM/dh < 0: ducting, or trapping as stronger evidence.
The strongest path names the likely interferer; ties go to the nearest.
One verdict per LRF and channel, naming the likely interferer.
e.g. TERH RF 31 · TRAPPING · WKMA-TV, 157 MI
start, update, ongoing every 5 min, clear
